en: The *Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-saptabuddha-dhāraṇī-mantra-sūtra*.
Translator unknown; now appended to the Liang dynasty catalog.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was dwelling on Mount Kailāsa, atop its summit, among all...
He dwelt in the celestial abode,
not far from the various worthy sages,
surrounded before and behind by a great assembly.
There were five hundred fully ordained bhikṣus,
and there were also five hundred great bodhisattvas together with them,
among whom was the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
Gaganagañja Bodhisattva,
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
and Akṣayapuṣpa Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, together with five hundred bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all of whom were in their final birth before buddhahood (ekajātipratibaddha), was present.
At that time, the World-Honored One gazed toward the four directions.
Not far from his dwelling place,
he saw a bhikṣu in the forest who was possessed by an evil spirit and was uttering various kinds of wicked words.
Within that grove, there was also another bhikṣu who exposed his body and raised both hands,
emitting various strange sounds from his mouth.
Some cried out to heaven and others called upon the earth;
at that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja,
having heard their voices, [acted] through the spiritual power of the Buddha.
Having adjusted his robes and knelt with his right knee on the ground,
he joined his palms toward the Buddha and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, these two bhikṣus..."
With what intention did you utter such a sound,
or raise both hands and further produce these harsh words?
Thereupon, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
This one bhikṣu, possessed by a malignant disease, uttered these sounds;
another bhikṣu, possessed by a malevolent spirit, ran about naked.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha—
He addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
it is for the sake of curing all the illnesses of sentient beings,
and for the sake of eliminating all evil spirits so that obstacles and difficulties do not arise."
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will, for the sake of all sentient beings,
expound a dhāraṇī mantra. At that time,
the World-Honored One manifested his majestic spiritual power.
In the midst of the void, six Buddhas immediately appeared.
Then, Śākyamuni Buddha ascended into the sky and sat in sequence with them.
At that time, the entire great assembly beheld the seven World-Honored Ones, the Buddhas.
At that time, Vipaśyin Buddha, for the sake of all sentient beings and to eliminate all obstacles and difficulties caused by malevolent spirits,
preached this Great Majestic Virtue Dhāraṇī Mantra.
And he spoke this mantra:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo vipaśye tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | oṃ hārā hārā hiri hīrāya | namo kirikirāya | yogāvacanāya | namo namaḥ svāhā.* At that time, Vipaśyin Buddha—
He addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"If there are good men or good women who receive and uphold this mantra,
whether reading it or reciting it..."
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who seeks out this mantra,
or one who delights in hearing it,
that person shall not be harmed by any blades or weapons.
They shall not be drowned by any water;
they shall not be seized by any suffering or affliction;
and they shall not undergo any untimely death.
Furthermore, if anyone should give poison to one who holds this mantra,
that poison shall transform into delicious food and not affect the person.
Moreover, if anyone should drink or eat [it], [the same shall occur].
First recite the mantra seven times and then eat. Once you have eaten,
all those who practice sorcery, those with evil speech,
and all manner of malevolent spirits will naturally vanish and be unable to cause harm.
If one upholds this dhāraṇī,
it will cause their lifespan to be extended;
whatever they practice and recite, they will comprehend upon hearing it once and never forget it.
One will constantly see the image of the Buddha day and night.
Furthermore, if there is someone who has been struck by a malevolent spirit and cannot recover,
[one should place it] by that person's ear.
If one recites the mantra seven times, the ailment will be immediately cured.
If there is someone suffering from *tuānfēng* (round-wind), white ringworm, or epilepsy, one should take *sūmàn* (soman),
green *shuǐxiāng* (aquatic fragrance), lotus flowers, cumin, and *xìxīn* (achyranthes).
Take equal portions of each and boil them in sesame oil.
By massaging the afflicted area with it, one will be immediately cured.
This applies to all those who have any ailment whatsoever.
By using this mantra to recite over them, there will be no failure to achieve recovery.
At that time, Śikhin Buddha was in the air;
desiring to eliminate all illnesses for the sake of all sentient beings, he [proceeded].
In order to eliminate all obstacles and difficulties caused by malevolent spirits,
he spoke this mantra:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo śikhinetratathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | oṃ paṭa paṭa paṭayā sarvabuddhanamaskṛtāya pratividdhāya svāhā.* At that time, Śikhin Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
I now proclaim this divine mantra, which has been spoken by hundreds of thousands of nayutas of countless billions of Buddhas;
I do so for the sake of all sentient beings and to eliminate all illnesses.
For the purpose of eliminating all obstacles and difficulties caused by malevolent spirits;
for the purpose of eliminating all evil dreams;
and for the purpose of eliminating all untimely deaths and illnesses.
He further addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"If there are good sons or good daughters who recite this mantra three times during the day and three times at night,"
Furthermore, if one brings to mind all forms of sorcery,
poison, malevolent incantations, curses, foul speech, and malicious tongues,
as well as all manner of yakṣas and māras, none shall be able to approach.
During the watches of the night, he constantly beholds all the Buddhas;
whatever food or drink he consumes is spontaneously digested and provides him with strength.
When that person’s life comes to an end, [he shall...]
All the Buddhas seen during the darkness of night will come to welcome one’s spirit and will constantly follow one wherever one goes.
Furthermore, if there are those who rely on this dhāraṇī method to manifest its efficacy, [the same shall occur].
For all illnesses, one must tie a consecrated mantra-cord.
If there is someone suffering from a severe illness,
take *sumana* wood and fry it in oil.
If one rubs their body with it, all ailments shall be healed.
If there are sentient beings who experience terror day and night,
one should take pure water, recite the mantra over it, and sprinkle it in the four directions.
If one fashions a mantra-cord and ties it upon their body,
no malevolent spirits (bhūtas) shall find an opportunity to harm them.
If there is a child who has been struck by an evil ghost, [this shall likewise protect them].
If one uses green thread to make a mantra-cord and ties it beneath the neck, one will immediately be healed.
Furthermore, if there is someone who has been struck by a malevolent spirit...
If one recites the mantra seven times by the side of the ear, one will also achieve recovery.
Whatever one desires to accomplish according to one's heart, there is nothing that cannot be achieved.
At that time, Vipaśyin Buddha was in the midst of the void.
It is because they desire to eliminate all illnesses for the sake of all sentient beings,
to eliminate all malevolent spirits,
and to prevent obstacles and difficulties from arising.
And he spoke this mantra:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo viśvabhuve tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | oṃ galā galā galā galā | kurū kurū kurū kurū | kurucetane | kuru sarvāghān | svāhā* At that time, after Viśvabhū Buddha had spoken this mantra, [he passed away].
He addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"Regarding this divine mantra, among the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, the Buddhas of the past have already spoken it;
the Buddhas of the present now speak it."
The Buddhas of the future shall speak it.
Furthermore, he addressed the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"You should receive and uphold this mantra."
If, in future ages, there are sentient beings who receive and uphold this mantra— whether reading it or reciting it—
or if there are others who seek out this mantra;
They shall not be terrified by swords or staves; they shall be free from all malevolent poisons, all fevers, and all drowning in water.
They shall not suffer untimely death nor be afflicted by malignant diseases.
All such [obstacles] shall be entirely eliminated;
only karmic retribution from past lives will not be removed.
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās...
Rising at dawn, bathe and wash your head and face.
Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times before the Buddha;
then no evil whatsoever shall befall your person.
All illnesses will naturally be cured;
one's lifespan will be extended, and all wealth and treasures will naturally become abundant;
all obstacles, hindrances, and unwholesome matters within the body will each be eliminated.
All enemies will naturally reconcile;
all curses and incantations shall not take hold upon one's person.
Such blessings as these are obtained through the causal conditions of bathing and reciting mantras.
If there are those who, in places of peril, difficulty, and fear,
are able to recollect this mantra, they shall all be freed from terror. Furthermore,
if there are those engaged in strife and contention, [they shall likewise be liberated].
To act as an advocate for the magistrate,
one should tie a mantra-cord made of white thread after reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times, and fasten it upon the person's right arm.
If anyone suffers from eye pain,
they should tie a mantra-empowered cord made from orange peel around their ear.
If enemies from another region intend to invade the borders, [one should likewise act].
Mix equal portions of ghee, curd, honey, and sesame seeds together.
Before an image of the Buddha, using a copper ladle, recite the mantra once for each ladleful and cast it into the fire, continuing this until one thousand and eight repetitions have been completed.
These enemies and bandits will naturally retreat and disperse, regardless of whether they are far or near.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who wishes to seek long life,
one should use curd and honey to fry non-glutinous rice into flowers.
Divide the three types [of substances] into equal portions.
Before the Buddha, roll them together with a copper tube, recite the mantra once for each roll, and cast them into the fire; repeat this one thousand and eight times.
Only then does one cease. Furthermore, there are those who,
for their own sake and for the sake of others, [seek to practice].
For those who wish to eliminate all fears and all transgressions; for those who seek all forms of prosperity, wealth, and treasures;
and for those who wish to remove obstacles and difficulties within their bodies to attain purity.
Furthermore, if there are those who wish to recite and uphold this mantra,
all fears, obstacles, and difficulties will be naturally eliminated, and their undertakings will be accomplished. Moreover,
for those who rely upon any dharma of mantras, [this shall likewise be so].
One shall also achieve accomplishment.
No enemies whatsoever shall find an opportunity against them.
If there is anyone who wishes to perform this rite:
When it is necessary to compound a medicinal ointment for application to the body, one requires fennel,
rice, nāgadantī, śrīparṇī, agallochum, śrīveṣṭaka, and saffron.
One requires kushtha, indravāruṇī, and the bodhi tree;
these and other such medicinal substances should be combined in equal parts.
Rising early in the morning, one should bathe for purification and anoint the body with medicinal ointments.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who wishes to see the king or a high minister,
they must burn citron wood before the image.
To use for fire, take a pinch of sesame seeds with the five fingers,
recite the mantra once, and cast it into the fire.
Do this one thousand and eight times before ceasing.
If there are good men or good women who wish to cause all enemies to naturally reach a state of reconciliation,
they should bathe themselves clean and put on pure garments.
At the hour of midnight, one should stand before the Buddha and make offerings of incense and flowers.
One should parch non-glutinous rice to form the flowers and take wood from the *karka* tree to kindle the fire.
Grasp a pinch of rice flowers with three fingers,
recite the mantra once, and cast them into the fire.
Do this one thousand and eight times, and then cease.
If there are good men or good women who, at night, see evil dreams; or if enemies seek to find their weak points;
or if all their undertakings fail to succeed; [they should recite this mantra].
On the morning of the fourteenth day, one must not eat at all.
When evening arrives, one should bathe the body with fragrant water, put on new and clean clothes,
and recite the mantra before the Buddha.
According to one's capacity, there is no limit to the amount;
one should simply continue with all one's strength until reaching the goal,
and must not leave the ritual site (*maṇḍala*).
He continued to sleep before the image until the morning of the fifteenth day,
when he immediately arose, washed himself clean, filled a cauldron with pure water, and prepared a bath.
Within that decoction, one must take renowned herbs and plants;
various [ingredients] should be added according to their availability,
and then the herbs should be strained out.
Then, take cloves, red sandalwood, and white sandalwood,
grind them into a powder,
and add them to the hot water according to the appropriate proportions.
Take two copper basins, each with a capacity of five *dō*,
fill them with scented water,
and place them before the image.
Having completed one thousand and eight recitations of the mantra,
one should immediately bathe the body with this decoction;
only then should one eat.
Furthermore, if there is someone who has been poisoned by a toxic substance,
one must cut purple *khadira* wood into pieces an inch long, as thick as a sinew, making one thousand and eight segments,
and smear them with cow dung.
Light a fire before the image.
Take a piece of wood, recite the mantra over it once,
and cast it into the fire one thousand and eight times.
Thereupon he would stop.
He would call out the patient's name and say,
"For that person, I shall eliminate the medicinal poison," and immediately the illness would be cured.
The efficacy of this mantra cannot be fully described.
Whatever one desires to accomplish in the mind,
there is nothing that will not be achieved by relying on this mantra-method.
At that time, Krakucchanda Buddha was in the air;
for the sake of removing all illnesses from all sentient beings and for the sake of removing all obstacles and difficulties caused by malevolent spirits.
And he spoke this mantra:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo Krakucchandāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | Oṃ ghaṭa ghaṭa ghaṭa ghaṭa | kīrti kīrti kīrti kīrti | namo sarvatathāgatavidyārājñe arhate samyaksaṃbuddhavidye | svāhā.* At that time, having spoken this mantra, the Buddha Krakucchanda [ceased].
He addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, saying:
"This mantra has already been spoken by as many Buddhas named Krakucchanda as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River; I now speak it."
I too praise this incantation’s inconceivable and immeasurable merit.
You should now receive and uphold it with a sincere heart.
If, in future ages, there should be anyone who receives and upholds this incantation, [they shall likewise attain such benefits].
Those who possess sincere faith and reverence for the Triple Gem should bathe with fragrant water, don new and clean garments,
and offer incense and flowers to the Buddha image.
Kneeling on the right knee with palms joined before the image,
recite the mantra one hundred and eight times;
within seven hundred lifetimes, you will personally know your past lives.
If one wishes to be born among the kings of the devas in the heavenly realms,
or if one is born among humans, one shall become a wheel-turning sage-king (cakravartin rāja),
provided one can uphold [this] daily.
When such a person’s life comes to an end, they will be reborn in the Land of Immeasurable Life and not be born among humans.
If a person recites this mantra day and night,
no accidental illnesses whatsoever shall afflict their body.
If one wishes to eat, one should first recite this mantra over it seven times;
thereafter, one may eat.
All diseases within the body will naturally be cured.
If there is anyone struck by any of the malevolent spirits, or possessed by them,
one should prepare fragrant incense water and recite this mantra over it one thousand and eight times.
Thereafter, use this decoction to bathe the patient.
Furthermore, recite this mantra over the patient one thousand and eight times.
Their illness will then be cured.
Furthermore, if there is a person whose body has developed malignant sores,
one should take a sharp iron blade and recite the mantra over this patient;
one should also take a copper needle and recite the mantra over it.
Thereafter, if one applies the needle to this sore, it will be immediately healed.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who has been bound in any prison or confinement,
one should recite this mantra over their hand seven times and rub their own face with it.
All official matters will naturally be resolved.
If a person constantly upholds this mantra,
all their wealth and possessions will naturally become sufficient, with nothing lacking.
All obstacles and difficulties will immediately be extinguished.
If anyone desires to see the Buddha,
they should purify their dwelling and smear the floor with fragrant mud.
Install an image of the Buddha and suspend silk banners and canopies;
offer incense, flowers, and other offerings;
bathe the body with fragrant water and don clean garments.
Burn aloeswood incense before the image;
kneel with the right knee on the ground and face directly east,
while the image faces west.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Upon finishing the recitation, lie down to sleep before the image with your head facing east.
Within that dream, they immediately behold the Buddha;
whatever thoughts arise in their minds at that time, they see them instantly.
Or, if they contemplate the length of their own lifespan, they immediately come to know it for themselves.
Or when one contemplates whether their own body is ill or healthy, they see it at that very moment;
or when there are enemies engaged in conflict and contention, they know the victory or defeat—
all such things as these are known.
At that time, they will know all that the mind contemplates;
having experienced this dream,
all obstacles, difficulties, and illnesses within their bodies [will be cleared away].
All [afflictions] were completely eliminated without remainder.
At that time, the Buddha Kanakamuni was in mid-air,
desiring to remove all illnesses for the sake of all sentient beings.
In order to eliminate all obstacles and difficulties caused by malevolent spirits,
he spoke this mantra:

Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Namo saṃghāya | Namo kanakamunaye tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | Oṃ sara sara sara sara | sirili sirili sirili sirili | sirāpāye | dhama dhama dhama dhama | dhumu dhumu dhumu dhumu | dhūmapāye | namo nāgakanakamunaye tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | svasti te maṇḍalapāra svāhā. At that time, the Buddha Kanakamuni addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
If any son or daughter of good family receives,
upholds, copies, and circulates this dhāraṇī,
they will remain far removed from all enemies, who shall find no opportunity to harm them.
Fire cannot burn them, and water cannot drown them.
They cannot be approached by thunder, lightning, or thunderbolts.
If someone were to give poison to one who maintains this mantra, [it would have no effect].
When such a person eats it, it is like consuming a savory soup or meal;
it naturally dissolves and transforms without any toxic vapors,
and one will not be subject to the terrors of untimely death or other calamities.
All that is consumed enters the abdomen and is naturally digested;
one attains a fine complexion, strength, and long life.
One is perpetually wealthy and noble, with riches and treasures appearing spontaneously.
All Buddhas will remember and protect them.
If a person has heavy karma from the three obstacles of the past,
by reciting this mantra three times daily, it shall be immediately eliminated.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who wishes to treat their own illness or the illness of others,
they should thoroughly clean the dwelling, smear the floor with fragrant mud,
hang silk banners and canopies, arrange a high seat, and install an image of the Buddha.
That person bathes their body with fragrant water and burns incense such as aloeswood and frankincense;
they prepare various kinds of vegetarian offerings according to their means to present to the Buddha.
If a patient stands before the image, one should recite the name of the patient while chanting the mantra; they will immediately be healed.
This applies even when all manner of ghosts, spirits, or *wangliang* have possessed a person.
If one uses this mantra to consecrate scented water for bathing the body, [the ailment] will be eliminated of its own accord. Furthermore,
if there is a person whose body suffers from *maṇḍala-vāta*, white leprosy, or leprosy,
one should take one *śeṣa* of sweet flag root (*achyranthes aspera*), pound it into a powder, and [use] one *āḍhaka*.
Mix it with white honey.
Before an image, recite the mantra over it one thousand and eight times.
This should be done at dawn before eating.
If one takes a square-inch spoonful daily, one will immediately be cured;
furthermore, all other chronic ailments such as deep-seated phlegm and indigestion will also be cured.
If there are those suffering from diseases of alternating cold and heat, [this shall likewise be applied].
It may bloom once every four days, or once every three days,
or once every two days, or once every day. One takes these various flowers to fashion them into a crown.
If one recites this mantra one thousand and eight times before an image [of the Buddha],
and pierces it through the head of the patient, the person shall immediately be healed.
Furthermore, if there is someone who has been struck by an evil spirit...
With the mouth closed and remaining silent,
one should recite the mantra in a low voice one hundred and eight times by the ear of the patient; then they will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, if there is anyone struck by a *vetāla* spirit,
or by a *pūtana*, a *kāṭapūtana*, a *piśāca*, a *kumbhāṇḍa*, or any other such malevolent spirits;
Take the flowers offered upon the Buddha’s body,
recite the mantra over them one thousand and eight times,
and burn them to fumigate the patient’s nose.
If its smoke enters the nose, one will immediately be cured.
Whatever one has in mind shall all be accomplished.
Such are the efficacious powers of this mantra; they cannot be fully described.
At that time, Kāśyapa Buddha was in the midst of the void.
Desiring to eliminate all evil diseases for the sake of sentient beings,
and to remove all obstacles and difficulties caused by malevolent spirits, he [manifested].
And he spoke this mantra:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | oṃ hrala hrala hrala hrala | ha ha ha | namo kāśyapāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | svasti me bhavatu mandalaprāpte svāhā.* At that time, Kāśyapa Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
This mantra of mine was spoken by as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
I have now finished speaking it;
you should now receive, uphold, read, and recite it.
One should recollect this day and night without allowing it to be forgotten.
In future ages, if there are good sons or good daughters who receive and uphold this mantra,
they should recite it three times during the course of a single day.
According to the extent of one's capacity,
that person shall behold all the Buddhas during the vigil of the dark night;
if they attain this vigil, all grave offenses will naturally be extinguished.
If there are those who have committed the five heinous crimes and do not believe in the Mahāyāna,
such grave offenses are otherwise beyond rescue; yet,
once this mantra has been recited, all their undertakings shall be fully accomplished.
For all types of skin eruptions, white leprosy, ringworm, and other such ailments,
take the flowers offered to the Buddha and recite the mantra over them one thousand and eight times before the image.
Grind them into a powder and mix it with cold water.
If one applies it to the afflicted area, the illness will be immediately cured;
it is also effective when mixed with cold water and drunk.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who suffers from a headache, [the same remedy should be applied].
Take the finest flowers for the Buddha and place them before the image;
recite the mantra over them one thousand and eight times,
then pound them into a paste and mix it with cold water.
Divide it into three portions and apply them to the head;
once they have dried, apply them again in this manner three times, and one will achieve a complete cure.
If a woman experiences difficult labor during childbirth:
Take the finest flowers offered to the Buddha, grind them into a powder,
mix them with cow’s ghee, and fry the mixture.
Once the frying is complete, place it before the image.
Recite this mantra one thousand and eight times and apply it to the birth canal;
the child will be born easily and the mother’s body will be restored to its normal state.
If the heavens rain excessively and do not clear, [recite it likewise].
Take the finest flowers and place them before the Buddha;
recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Then, go to an open space and burn them, and the affliction will immediately be ceased and eliminated.
Furthermore, if there is a person struck by a malevolent ghost,
their mouth becomes clenched and they cannot speak; or if they are struck by a piśāca ghost.
If one suffers from chronic ailments or disorders of dampness,
one should take flowers offered to the Buddha,
pound them into a powder, and mix it with wine, such as grape wine or rice wine.
Place it in a silver bowl before the image and recite the mantra one thousand and eight times;
give it to the patient to consume, and they will immediately be cured.
All undertakings whatsoever will be fully accomplished by reciting this mantra one thousand and eight times before the image.
If one wishes to perform any task, [one should do so].
Recite this mantra and do not give rise to doubt.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha was in the midst of the void,
desiring to eliminate all illnesses for the sake of sentient beings.
In order to eliminate all obstacles and difficulties caused by malevolent spirits,
he spoke this mantra: Namo Buddhāya.
Namo dharmāya, namo saṃghāya, namo śākyamunaye.
Tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya tadyathā.
Kumiti kumiti mahākumiti.
Tare tare mahātare care care.
Mahācāre cāre cāre mahācāre.
Tiri tiri mahātiri haha.
Kili kili mahākili cūḷa cūḷa.
Mahā-cūḍā-mi-li mi-li mahā-mi-li.
Tiri tiri mahātiri dhumi dhumi.
Mahā-tu-mi-cara-le cara-le mahā-cara-le.
Kili kili mahākili cili cili.
Mamajili svāhā.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
If there are good men or good women who receive,
uphold, read, recite, and constantly mindfully contemplate this mantra day and night,
that person shall not be threatened by any fear of swords, staves, or the like.
One shall not be afflicted by any malignant diseases,
nor shall one undergo any untimely death.
This is the efficacy as described by the six Buddhas mentioned previously.
"This mantra of mine is likewise thus, without any difference. Then,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja addressed the Buddha,
saying, "World-Honored One..."
I now wish to speak of the mantra;
because it protects the divine mantras spoken by the seven Buddhas,
I shall therefore speak of it once more.
This mantra is able to destroy all karmic obstacles and hindrances.
It is recited as follows:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | ākāśagarbhāya | bodhisattvāya | mahāsattvāya | mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | cili cili | mahācili | doulou doulou | mahādoulou | jialili jialili | mahājialili | heli heli | mahāheli | svāhā.* I shall now describe the functional power of this mantra.
If a person is struck by a malevolent spirit,
one must tie a mantra-cord and recite the mantra over it one thousand and eight times.
Take *sumana* wood, ghee, and mustard seeds, and mix these three ingredients in equal portions.
Before the patient, take a pinch with three fingers;
recite the mantra once and cast it into the fire.
Continue in this manner for one thousand and eight times, then cease.
Their illness will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who, being terrified, wishes to establish a boundary (*sīmābandha*),
they should take a blade and recite the mantra over it one thousand and eight times.
Place it facing the door.
If one is in mid-air establishing a boundary to ward off evil spirits seeking an opportunity,
one should take water, recite the mantra over it seven times, and sprinkle it in the four directions.
If one has fear within oneself,
one should bind a mantra-cord to protect one's own body.
If there is someone who has been affected by poison, [one should likewise act].
Take *gu-lu* grass;
if one uses it to recite mantras over a patient, they will immediately be cured.
If there is anyone with a wind-related illness (*vāta-roga*), [the same applies].
If one recites the mantra over scented oil one thousand and eight times and applies it to the afflicted area, the illness will be immediately cured.
If there is anyone suffering from earache, [the same shall apply].
Take *agaru* (Aquilaria) incense and fry it in oil;
by pouring this into the ears, one will immediately be cured.
If a person suffers from abdominal pain:
Recite the mantra for black salt one hundred and eight times;
give it to the patient to consume, and they will immediately be cured.
If there is anyone suffering from toothache, [the same applies].
Take *sumanā* water and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times.
Crush it and use it to brush the teeth, and the pain will be immediately relieved.
If there is a child who cries out in terror day and night, [use this method].
Take white thread to fashion a mantra-cord;
recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times.
Tying it beneath the neck of a child will immediately eliminate their fear.
If anyone suffers from a headache,
they should take a blade of tempered steel or use their hand, reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times over it;
by rubbing it upon the head, the affliction will be immediately cured.
If there is anyone who has been subjected to the malevolent incantations or curses of others,
one should take a blade of tempered iron for seven days and seven nights;
by using this to recite the mantra over the patient, they will immediately be cured.
If thunder and lightning should strike,
one should break off a branch of a pomegranate tree by hand,
without removing the thorns or leaves.
Holding it in one's hand, one should go toward the place where the sound originates;
by reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times, it will be immediately eliminated.
This applies to all activities one wishes to perform.
When reciting this dhāraṇī, one must first offer incense and flowers;
thereafter, there will be no failure in achieving success.
Having spoken this sutra, [the Buddha said:]
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, along with the eight classes of beings,
including devas and nāgas, were simultaneously filled with joy and offered praise;
they single-mindedly received and practiced [the teaching].
The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī Mantras of the Seven Buddhas as Asked by the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
